claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: Failing scans unconditionally when the index is behind the tip breaks scans for ranges that are already available.
claims.quote: There we don't fail unconditionally if the index isn't synced. We only fail if we the range isn't available.

status_by.quote: You're right - thanks. getblockfilter does not fail merely because index is behind the tip, so it fails when the request

claims.status_note: author updated to mirror getblockfilter and only fail when the requested range is unavailable

claims.author: fjahr
claims.quote: This doesn't make sense, you are waiting for the index to be synced just to delete it without doing anything else.
claims.request: Remove the redundant wait for the index to sync right before deleting it.

status_by.quote: Agreed, that was pointless, so the new version does not delete the index at all.

claims.status_note: author agreed and stopped deleting the index in the updated test

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: The functional test mines an excessive number of blocks.
claims.quote: No normal functional test should require mining this many blocks.

status_by.quote: I agree, the new test does not depend on timing anymore, it mines 100 blocks, which is the minimum needed to build the regtest snapshot chain

claims.status_note: author rewrote the test using an assumeutxo snapshot, reducing mining to 100 blocks

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: The functional test relies on races and is non-deterministic.
claims.quote: And we don't leave the actual testing to chance. The test either needs to work deterministically or it is of no use for us, with maybe some very rare exceptions.

status_by.quote: Thanks, this was the right hint and the new test does exactly that: node2 loads the regtest snapshot while it has no peers, so its filter index stays at height 199 while the active tip is at 299.

claims.status_note: author rewrote the test using an assumeutxo snapshot without peers to avoid timing dependencies

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: Index readiness checked before the scan begins may become outdated by the end of a long scan, leading to misclassified errors.
claims.quote: This status may be outdated at the end of a long scan.

status_by.quote: Agreed. The flag is gone. The state of the index is now read at the moment the lookup fails, with GetSummary()

claims.status_note: author removed the cached index_ready flag and checks index state at failure time via GetSummary()

claims.author: fjahr
claims.question: Why throw an error when a filter range is unavailable instead of returning a partial result?
claims.quote: Why throw here instead of returning a partial result?

status_by.quote: I thought about it and chose the error for these reasons: 1. "completed" is documented as "true if the scan was not aborted".

claims.status_note: author explained why returning partial results would be problematic and asked reviewer to clarify preference
